info.title: transit-data service
info.description:
Timetable lifecycle: GTFS import (raw -> staging -> core), H3 grid and access stops,
activation of a feed version, and the timetable artifacts consumed by `accessibility`.
Owns schemas `transit` and `transit_staging`.

`x-access`: access level at the gateway (`internal` = not routed). `x-rate-limit`: per-minute
limit at the gateway.

post.summary: Download the feed of a source and import it
post.description:
Answers at once with a `downloading` feed version; everything else (download, staging,
promotion, transfers, access stops) runs in the background, however long it takes: poll
`GET /admin/feed-versions/{id}`. A download that fails, or an archive that was imported before,
ends as `failed` with the reason in `errorMessage`.

202.description: The import runs in the background.

Location.description: URL of the created or running resource.

duplicate.description: true = this archive had been imported before (no-op).

403.description: The caller is authenticated but not allowed to do this.

get.summary: Timetable artifact for one service date
get.description:
Trips whose service runs on `date`, plus trips of the previous day still running after
midnight (their times minus 86 400). Grouped into non-overtaking patterns. Built once per
(feed version, date) and cached; sent gzip-compressed with a strong `ETag`.

schema.description: Format of `docs/05-algorithms.md#4-timetable-artifact-transit-data---accessibility`.

stops.description: Stops in id order; `id` is the compact stop id used everywhere else in the artifact.

trips.description:
One array per trip, `[arr0, dep0, arr1, dep1, ...]` in seconds of the service day
(negative for the part of a previous-day trip before midnight). Sorted by the
departure at the first stop; trips never overtake each other within a pattern.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of the problem kind.

detail.description: Explanation specific to this occurrence. Never contains SQL, stack traces or personal data.

instance.description: Request path that produced the problem.

correlationId.description: Same value as the `X-Correlation-Id` response header.

errors.description: Field errors of a validation problem.

path.description: JSON pointer of the invalid field, e.g. `/origin/lat`.

Forbidden.description: The caller is authenticated but not allowed to do this.

X-Correlation-Id.description: Correlation id of the request (received or generated).
